title: Beetles of Russia and Western Europe, plate 26: Lucanus cervus (male, fig. 14) among other lucanids and scarabs
creator: Georgiy Jacobson (author); chromolithograph plates after Calwers Kaeferbuch and drawings by O. Somina
institution: A. F. Devrien, St. Petersburg; scan via the Zoological Institute RAS (zin.ru) and Wikimedia Commons
license: Public domain (published 1905-1915, author died 1926; Wikimedia Commons PD-old)
attribution: Jacobson, G. G. (1905-1915). Zhuki Rossii i Zapadnoj Evropy (Beetles of Russia and Western Europe), plate 26. St. Petersburg: A. F. Devrien. Scan via Wikimedia Commons.
notes: Chromolithograph plate, 22 beetles on white paper. Fig. 14, the male stag beetle (Lucanus cervus), is a large dorsal view with full mandibles, antennae and six legs, centred around x 0.35-0.75, y 0.30-0.71 of the plate. Cut into the boss rig parts by hand mattes: body, head, two mandibles, two antennae, two front legs.
